scope: write the first working piece of our own game server and self-test it

created.description: UDP game-server skeleton for protocol generation 1.1.1.13: logs every datagram and answers the three out-of-band commands the client uses during startup

self_test.client_probe: raw UDP datagrams prefixed with ffffffff

what_it_logs.inbound_inband: sequence, length, first 64 bytes as hex (not parsed yet)
what_it_logs.outbound: text and full hex of every reply
what_it_logs.parsed_connect: uid, userinfo keys, name, xuid, challenge field, build field
what_it_logs.counters: oob/inband received and sent, per-command counts

deliberately_not_done_yet: any lobby/auth behaviour (server319 keeps that role)
how_it_fits: the 1649370 client writes packets into an in-process ring, so tools/ring_bridge_1649370.py forward drains the ring and speaks UDP; this server is the UDP peer the bridge forwards to. Next step is to point the bridge at port 28971 instead of the 2697 dedrun on 28970 and watch a real client handshake.
next: run a real 1649370 session with forward --target 127.0.0.1:28971 and confirm the server logs the client's getchallenge/connect/stats with real fields
compare the captured challenge/connect/connectResponse fields with what the 2697 dedrun saw, to expose any 3.19.26.22 differences
then add the in-band netchan layer (decode first, reply later)
